title: @csp/privacy PII detection/removal + k-anonymity + fail-closed invariant
context: Privacy is a first-class, fail-closed module: no living-individual PII ever leaves a pipeline, and when detection is uncertain the pipeline generalizes harder or halts rather than leaking. This package detects and removes/pseudonymizes observer PII and runs a quasi-identifier k>=5 check, enforced by an invariant test on outputs. Per Hee-Lee Oss guardrails, identity-level data is de-identified, never retained. Depends on csp-engine-002 and the csp-policy-003 charter.
objective: Implement @csp/privacy PII detection/removal (names, emails, usernames, precise home coordinates, device IDs) with a quasi-identifier k>=5 check and a fail-closed invariant test asserting no denylisted PII field and no finer-than-permitted coordinate appears in any output.
acceptanceCriteria: Detects and removes/pseudonymizes living-individual PII (names, emails, usernames, precise home coords, device IDs); runs a quasi-identifier k>=5 check
Fail-closed invariant test: no output contains a denylisted PII field, and no coordinate finer than its record's permitted precision
On detection uncertainty the pipeline coarsens to the coarsest configured level or halts (never emits finer precision on doubt)
Test fixtures are synthetic or trivially public only; no real PII committed to repo or CI
output: A PR adding the @csp/privacy package with PII detection/removal, the k-anonymity check, and the passing fail-closed invariant test.
